trigger: a release-prep author or reader of changelog.d/README.md meets two contradictory rules in one file and the hook gives a third
summary: changelog.d/README.md:3 'Never edit CHANGELOG.md in a PR' and :48 'Never touch CHANGELOG.md itself' have no exception; 'the release owner approves it in the PR' has no role definition or independence requirement (the approver could be the author); 'After the tag the section is closed' is ambiguous against the next subsection 'Fixes that land after a version was promoted' (promote --append after an RC tag); hook REASON still says a released-section typo fix is 'operator-owned: ask the user, who can approve a Bash-based edit'; .claude/skills/release/SKILL.md never mentions the carve-out; CONTRIBUTING.md:132 and .github/pull_request_template.md:19 and CLAUDE.md:228 / AGENTS.md:243 say never (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md need no change if the owner PR route is used; they defer to this file). containment (every hunk inside one section) and 'corrects a fact, adds no claim' are honour-system: assemble-changelog.py --check lints fragments only, --guard compares only [Unreleased], test_changelog_order.py checks header order/dates (chaos-injector injected a bullet into the closed 0.14.1 section and a new blockquote into 0.15.0 on scratch copies; --guard and --check passed both; a hunk-containment script caught only the 0.14.1 one). promote 0.15.0 --append preserves hand corrections and a plain re-promote refuses (chaos-injector, scratch copy; consistency-auditor read the code). Suggested text: line 3 add '(sole exception: the release-prep correction under "Correcting a promoted section on a release-prep branch" below)'; Rule 2 append ', except as that section allows'; carve-out: replace '(the release owner approves it in the PR)' with '(a maintainer other than the PR's author approves it in a PR comment that links the hunks; wording or guidance changes, not only facts, are named explicitly)', add 'a hunk corrects an existing statement and adds no new bullet or claim' and 'list the hunks with git diff -U0 <promote-commit> -- CHANGELOG.md and confirm each lies between that section's ## [X.Y.Z] header and the next ## [ (neither --guard nor --check looks outside [Unreleased])', and 'After the final tag'. Hook REASON add: 'Before the tag, a release-prep branch may hand-correct the section it just promoted (changelog.d/README.md, "Correcting a promoted section on a release-prep branch"); that needs maintainer approval. After the tag use a fragment.' A CI backstop (promote-output vs HEAD diff restricted to the section) is a follow-up, not a finding against this diff.
classification_rationale: new policy text under-specified and unreconciled

trigger: an existing 0.14.x customer reads the 0.15.0 docs and finds no statement of what to do next; the contract says there is no upgrade path and every new banner and README.md:193 point back at it; after 0.15.0 the banners ('for 0.15.0', 'an earlier build's') also read as covering 0.15.0 itself for a later 0.15.x
summary: OWNER DECISION, not author-fixable and not a finding against this diff under the scope ruling (the contract was set 2026-10-24); recorded so it is not lost. Suggested neutral paragraph for upgrading.md under the banner (enterprise-readiness; agent re-enrolment against a fresh CA was not verified): 'If you run 0.14.x today. 0.15.0 does not replace a 0.14.x deployment in place and ships no migration of its database, backups, enrollment tokens or secrets key. Keep the 0.14.x deployment in service until you have planned a separate, freshly provisioned 0.15.0 deployment.' Also decide the supported-upgrade commitment for 0.15.0 -> 0.15.x (revisit by 0.15.1) and whether CHANGELOG [0.15.0] needs a headline for the cutover. No issue filed by this run; disposition stays open. Further follow-ups observed (code/other, not this diff): the importer accepts credentials from an unattested file at any boot with no marker (consider an explicit opt-in or refusal when enrollment state already exists; owner call because the contract says provenance is not enforced); no alert ships for yuzu_server_enrollment_import_total{outcome=~"imported|fingerprint_mismatch|error"} and metrics.md:585 says 'Alert on any fingerprint_mismatch or error increase' (no such rule ships; an 'imported' outcome on a fresh deployment is itself the signal); scripts/yuzu-backup.sh:99-110 still collects the .cfg files as a pre-6.2 import source and yuzu-restore.sh:~104 copies *.cfg into the importer's search directory; a provenance stamp checked by the migration runner for S5 (earlier-build dump restored silently); README.md:193 'backs up nothing' about the 0.14.0 header recipe is imprecise (it backed up unprefixed, effectively empty volumes).
